name: Sustanon (testosterone blend)

lead: Sustanon is the brand name for mixed-ester testosterone injections. Sustanon 250 combines four esters (propionate, phenylpropionate, isocaproate and decanoate), and Sustanon 100 combines three. It is discussed in bodybuilding circles for building muscle and a fuller physique.

The chain: after intramuscular injection each ester is cleaved to release testosterone, with shorter esters acting sooner and longer ones lasting longer, so the blend spreads release over time. Testosterone's effects on lean mass are well documented in general. This specific blend has little published research of its own and no appearance trials.

paras: It is an injectable used in TRT and in bodybuilding circles, valued for mixing faster and slower release in one product. Muscle changes from testosterone build over weeks to months.
General testosterone risks include acne, sperm suppression, raised red blood cell counts and cardiovascular and prostate considerations. Testosterone is a controlled substance in many countries.

angle.text: Sustanon is a blended testosterone ester injection used in bodybuilding circles to build muscle and size by raising testosterone and protein synthesis. Testosterone's effect on lean mass is well documented; this blend has no appearance trials of its own.

lead: Sustanon is the brand name of a family of mixed-ester testosterone injections made by Organon. Sustanon 250 combines four testosterone esters (propionate, phenylpropionate, isocaproate and decanoate), and Sustanon 100 combines three of them (propionate, phenylpropionate and isocaproate).[1][2] It is a prescription testosterone replacement product, and it is also a long-standing name in bodybuilding circles, where testosterone is discussed for its effects on muscle mass and body composition, and so on how a physique looks.[2]

The idea behind the blend is staggered release: shorter esters act sooner and longer ones last longer, so one injection spreads testosterone out over time.[2][3] Wikipedia describes the usual medical schedule as every few weeks for Sustanon 250 and every two weeks for Sustanon 100, and notes the product is commonly prescribed for transmasculine people undergoing masculinising hormone therapy.[2]

In controlled research Sustanon 250 has been used in studies of testosterone and muscle: a double-blind trial in older men who combined it with resistance training reported greater fat-free mass gains and reduced fat mass than placebo.[4] No trial has examined Sustanon for cosmetic or appearance outcomes in healthy young men.

paras: Sustanon is given by intramuscular injection as testosterone replacement.[2] Wikipedia reports that brief UK shortages occurred in late 2011 and mid-2012 because of manufacturing changes, and that the product is commonly used in masculinising hormone therapy for trans men.[2] Reviews of testosterone replacement list intramuscular Sustanon among the clinically available delivery forms, alongside gels, patches and long-acting depot injections.[5]

Wikipedia describes Sustanon as a popular anabolic steroid among bodybuilders during bulking phases.[2] In forum discussions, such as T Nation threads, users compare it with other ester blends and debate how the esters behave when injected at different frequencies.[6][7] This wiki does not give dosing or injection guidance.

The esters are prodrugs: they are cleaved after injection to release testosterone, and their different elimination half-lives give a sustained but non-linear release from the oil depot.[2][3] Testosterone ester blends in oil are the most common injectable route for replacement therapy.[3]

Anti-doping researchers studied the detection of Sustanon esters in blood. In a six-person clinical study that included a single Sustanon injection, intact esters could be followed in serum and plasma over a 60-day sampling window, which gives a way to prove exogenous testosterone use.[8]

General testosterone-therapy effects include acne, oily skin and hair loss, suppression of sperm production, and warnings about cardiovascular events, prostate conditions and blood pressure; testosterone is contraindicated in pregnancy.[3] Injectable oil preparations can cause pulmonary oil microembolism, with cough and shortness of breath.[3]

In healthy young men, androgen treatment with Sustanon suppressed circulating testosterone, LH and the Leydig cell marker INSL3 in a study of testicular suppression, consistent with the shutdown of the body's own testosterone production.[9] A 2024 paper in Translational Andrology and Urology reported that Sustanon suppresses spermatogenesis and increases cell death.[10]

A 2019 randomised, double-blind trial gave 18 healthy older men Sustanon or saline injections during six weeks of resistance training. The testosterone group gained more total, leg and appendicular fat-free mass and lost more fat mass than placebo, with improvements in muscle thickness and cross-sectional area reported.[4]

Other human studies used Sustanon as an experimental tool, including a six-man study of testicular suppression and a six-participant study of how long injected esters stay detectable in blood.[8][9] No studies were found of Sustanon for appearance in healthy young adults.
